passages.text: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.
passages.original: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ πλούσιοι κλαύσατε ὀλολύζοντες ἐπὶ ταῖς ταλαιπωρίαις ὑμῶν ταῖς ἐπερχομέναις
passages.objections:
Why should I worry about anything bad happening to me just because I have wealth?
My riches are a sign that I’m favored and blessed, not that I should be afraid.
Nothing bad ever comes to those who are successful and powerful.
If I have money, I can avoid any trouble that might come my way.
Wealth protects me from misery, so I have nothing to fear.
I don’t see why I should feel sorry or anxious about my comfortable life.
Being rich means I’ve done everything right, so why would I need to weep?
Only the poor have to worry about suffering, not people like me.
If I’m enjoying prosperity now, that means I’ll always be secure.
There’s no reason for me to expect any hardship just because I’m wealthy.

passages.text: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.
passages.original: ὁ πλοῦτος ὑμῶν σέσηπεν καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια ὑμῶν σητόβρωτα γέγονεν
passages.objections:
I’ve worked hard for my wealth, so it will always keep me secure.
My fine clothes and possessions show that I’m blessed and favored.
As long as I have money and nice things, I don’t need to worry about the future.
My riches will last and provide for my family for generations.
If I just keep collecting more, I’ll finally be satisfied and happy.
Expensive clothes and treasures prove my worth to others.
Nothing bad can happen to me as long as I have plenty stored up.
It’s impossible for my wealth to lose its value or become useless.
I don’t need to think about what happens to my possessions after I’m gone.

passages.text: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire. You have hoarded treasure in the last days.
passages.original: ὁ χρυσὸς ὑμῶν καὶ ὁ ἄργυρος κατίωται καὶ ὁ ἰὸς αὐτῶν εἰς μαρτύριον ὑμῖν ἔσται καὶ φάγεται τὰς σάρκας ὑμῶν ὡς πῦρ Ἐθησαυρίσατε ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις
passages.objections:
If I just keep saving up more and more wealth, nothing bad will ever happen to me.
My riches will always protect me, no matter what comes.
It doesn’t matter if I hoard my money; it’s not hurting anyone.
Gold and silver can’t go bad—they’ll always be valuable.
I can store up as much treasure as I want, and it won’t have any consequences.
As long as I’m rich, I don’t need to worry about the future.
No one will ever judge me for how much I’ve accumulated.
Wealth is the best way to secure my life, especially when times get tough.
If I keep my riches to myself, I’ll be safe when the end comes.
There’s no harm in piling up treasures for myself while others struggle.

passages.text: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ ὁ μισθὸς τῶν ἐργατῶν τῶν ἀμησάντων τὰς χώρας ὑμῶν ὁ ἀφυστερημένος ἀφ’ ὑμῶν κράζει καὶ αἱ βοαὶ τῶν θερισάντων εἰς τὰ ὦτα Κυρίου Σαβαὼθ εἰσεληλύθασιν
passages.objections:
No one will ever know if I keep a little extra for myself and don’t pay the workers what I promised.
It’s not my problem if the laborers are struggling; I earned this land and their pay is up to me.
God doesn’t care about how I run my business or treat my workers.
The poor are used to hardship, so missing a day’s wage won’t hurt them.
If I don’t pay them now, they’ll just have to wait until I’m ready.
As long as I’m successful, it doesn’t matter if I cut corners with my employees.
Nobody is watching, so I can get away with underpaying the harvesters.
The cries of these workers are meaningless; no one important will listen to them.
I can always make it right later if I feel like it, but for now, I need the money more than they do.

passages.text: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.
passages.original: Ἐτρυφήσατε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐσπαταλήσατε ἐθρέψατε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σφαγῆς
passages.objections:
Why shouldn’t I enjoy all the pleasures I can while I’m alive? 
If I have the means, isn’t it right for me to indulge myself and live in comfort? 
There’s nothing wrong with spending my wealth on whatever makes me happy. 
As long as I’m not hurting anyone, why shouldn’t I live for my own satisfaction? 
Isn’t the purpose of life to seek as much luxury and enjoyment as possible? 
If I’ve worked hard for my riches, don’t I deserve to use them however I want? 
Why should I worry about the future when I can feast and celebrate today? 
Isn’t it wise to store up as much as I can and enjoy it before anything bad happens? 
If I’m successful, doesn’t that mean I’m favored and should reward myself?

passages.text: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.
passages.original: κατεδικάσατε ἐφονεύσατε τὸν δίκαιον οὐκ ἀντιτάσσεται ὑμῖν
passages.objections:
Those people deserved what happened to them—they were just in the way.
If someone is powerless, it means they’re not worth protecting.
No one will care if we get rid of the innocent; they can’t fight back anyway.
It’s fine to take advantage of the weak, since they can’t stop us.
Justice is only for those who can defend themselves.
If someone doesn’t resist, it must mean they’re guilty or weak.
We can do whatever we want to the righteous, since they won’t retaliate.
There’s no harm in condemning someone who won’t stand up for themselves.
If the innocent suffer, it’s just the way of the world.
No one will notice if we silence those who are good.

passages.text: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil—how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.
passages.original: Μακροθυμήσατε οὖν ἀδελφοί ἕως τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Κυρίου ἰδοὺ ὁ γεωργὸς ἐκδέχεται τὸν τίμιον καρπὸν τῆς γῆς μακροθυμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἕως λάβῃ πρόϊμον καὶ ὄψιμον
passages.objections:
I’m tired of waiting—nothing ever changes, so why bother being patient?
If the Lord was really coming, wouldn’t He have come by now?
I can’t see any reward for waiting, so I might as well take what I want now.
Patience is pointless when life is so unfair and hard.
Why should I wait for something I can’t see or prove?
Everyone else is getting ahead by looking out for themselves, not by waiting.
If God cared, He wouldn’t make us wait so long for justice.
I don’t have the strength to keep hoping for something that might never happen.
It’s better to act now than to wait for some promise in the future.
I’ve already waited long enough—surely I deserve answers right away.

passages.text: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.
passages.original: μακροθυμήσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς στηρίξατε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὅτι ἡ παρουσία τοῦ Κυρίου ἤγγικεν
passages.objections:
I don’t see the point in waiting any longer—nothing ever changes for us.
Why should I keep hoping when it feels like the Lord is never coming back?
I’m too tired to keep going; I just want to give up now.
If the Lord was really coming soon, wouldn’t things be easier for us?
I don’t have the strength to keep believing when everything seems so hopeless.
Why should I be patient when evil people keep getting away with everything?
It feels like God has forgotten about us, so why bother holding on?
I can’t keep my heart strong when I see so much suffering around me.
Maybe we’ve misunderstood—what if the Lord isn’t coming at all?
I don’t think waiting patiently will make any difference in my life.

passages.text: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!
passages.original: μὴ στενάζετε ἀδελφοί κατ’ ἀλλήλων ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε ἰδοὺ ὁ κριτὴς πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν ἕστηκεν
passages.objections:
I can’t help but grumble about the others—how else will things ever change?
If I don’t point out everyone’s faults, who will?
It’s just harmless venting; it doesn’t really matter if I complain about my brothers.
Everyone else is always complaining, so why shouldn’t I?
I’m justified in criticizing them because they’re always making mistakes.
It’s not a big deal to talk behind someone’s back if they’re not around.
I don’t see any harm in sharing my frustrations about others with the group.
If I don’t express my annoyance, I’ll just explode.
There’s no real consequence for complaining about others—it’s just words.
I have every right to judge my brothers when they mess up.

passages.text: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
passages.original: Ὑπόδειγμα λάβετε ἀδελφοί τῆς κακοπαθίας καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας τοὺς προφήτας οἳ ἐλάλησαν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Κυρίου
passages.objections:
Why should I keep going when things get tough? No one else has had to deal with what I’m facing.
I don’t see any point in being patient—nothing ever changes for the better.
If God really cared, He wouldn’t let His people suffer like this.
I’m sure those who serve God never had to endure hardship like I do.
Why should I bother staying faithful when it only brings me trouble?
People who speak for God should have easy lives, not suffering and pain.
If I’m struggling, it must mean I’ve done something wrong or God has abandoned me.
No one understands what I’m going through, so why should I look to others for encouragement?
There’s no value in enduring hardship; it just makes life miserable.
If God wanted me to be patient, He wouldn’t let bad things happen to me.

passages.text: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ μακαρίζομεν τοὺς ὑπομείναντας τὴν ὑπομονὴν Ἰὼβ ἠκούσατε καὶ τὸ τέλος Κυρίου εἴδετε ὅτι πολύσπλαγχνός ἐστιν ὁ Κύριος καὶ οἰκτίρμων
passages.objections:
I don’t see how anyone who suffers for a long time could ever be considered blessed.
If God really cared, He wouldn’t let good people go through so much pain.
There’s no point in being patient when nothing ever changes for the better.
I think God is too harsh and doesn’t show much mercy to those who struggle.
Why should I keep trusting when it seems like God never rewards perseverance?
People who go through trials must have done something wrong to deserve it.
I doubt that God actually cares about our suffering or wants to help us.
It’s impossible to believe that anything good can come from enduring hardship.
If God was truly compassionate, He would stop all suffering immediately.
I don’t think anyone who suffers a lot could ever be happy or blessed in the end.

passages.text: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.
passages.original: Πρὸ πάντων δέ ἀδελφοί μου μὴ ὀμνύετε μήτε τὸν οὐρανὸν μήτε τὴν γῆν μήτε ἄλλον τινὰ ὅρκον ἤτω δὲ ὑμῶν τὸ Ναὶ ναί καὶ τὸ Οὒ οὔ ἵνα μὴ ὑπὸ κρίσιν πέσητε
passages.objections:
If I really want people to believe me, I should swear by something important.
Sometimes you have to make a big oath to prove you’re telling the truth.
It’s not a big deal to swear by heaven or earth if I’m being honest.
People won’t trust me unless I make a strong promise or oath.
I can’t see any harm in swearing as long as I keep my word.
If I just say “yes” or “no,” folks might think I’m hiding something.
Making oaths is just part of how everyone does business around here.
God doesn’t care about the words I use as long as my intentions are good.
Swearing by something holy makes my promise more meaningful.
It’s only wrong to swear if you don’t mean it, right?

passages.text: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.
passages.original: Κακοπαθεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν προσευχέσθω εὐθυμεῖ τις ψαλλέτω
passages.objections:
When I’m suffering, there’s no point in praying—nothing will change.
If I’m happy, I don’t need to do anything special; singing or praising is unnecessary.
Prayer is only for big problems, not for everyday struggles or pain.
When things are going well, I should just enjoy it and not bother with spiritual things.
If I’m hurting, I should just tough it out on my own instead of turning to prayer.
Singing praises is only for church services, not for when I’m feeling good in daily life.
God doesn’t care about my personal feelings, whether I’m sad or happy.
There’s no use in praying when I’m suffering because it won’t make a difference.
I should only pray when I need something, not when I’m just feeling down.
If I’m cheerful, it’s because of my own efforts, so I don’t need to give thanks or praise.

passages.text: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
passages.original: ἀσθενεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν προσκαλεσάσθω τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ προσευξάσθωσαν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀλείψαντες αὐτὸν ἐλαίῳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου
passages.objections:
If someone is sick, there's nothing the church can do to help them.
Prayer doesn't make any difference when someone is ill.
Only doctors and medicine can help when you're sick, not spiritual leaders.
It's pointless to involve others in your personal health problems.
Anointing with oil is just an old superstition and has no real effect.
God doesn't care about our physical sickness, only our souls.
If you're sick, you should just suffer in silence and not bother anyone.
There's no reason to ask for prayer from others; it's a private matter.
The church has no role in healing or caring for the sick.
Sickness is just fate, and nothing spiritual can change it.

passages.text: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως σώσει τὸν κάμνοντα καὶ ἐγερεῖ αὐτὸν ὁ Κύριος κἂν ἁμαρτίας ᾖ πεποιηκώς ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ
passages.objections:
I don’t think prayer really does anything for someone who’s sick.
If you’ve messed up too badly, there’s no way you can be forgiven.
God doesn’t care enough to help people who are suffering.
Once you’re sick, it’s all up to the doctors—faith can’t change that.
If someone’s done wrong, they have to pay for it themselves, not just ask for forgiveness.
There’s no point in asking God for help; He won’t listen to people like us.
Some sins are just too big to be forgiven, no matter what you do.
Why bother praying when nothing ever changes?
If you’re really sick, it means God is punishing you and won’t help.
Only perfect people can expect God to answer their prayers.

passages.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.
passages.original: Ἐξομολογεῖσθε οὖν ἀλλήλοις τὰς ἁμαρτίας καὶ εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων ὅπως ἰαθῆτε πολὺ ἰσχύει δέησις δικαίου ἐνεργουμένη
passages.objections:
I don’t need to tell anyone about my mistakes; it’s just between me and God.
Praying for others doesn’t really make a difference in their lives.
No one else needs to know about my struggles—I can handle them alone.
Confessing my sins to someone else is pointless and embarrassing.
Only special people’s prayers matter; mine won’t help anyone.
If I admit my faults to others, they’ll just judge me and nothing good will come of it.
There’s no real power in prayer; it’s just words.
I can’t be healed or helped by someone else’s prayers.
Righteous people aren’t any different from the rest of us when it comes to prayer.
It’s better to keep my problems to myself rather than burden others.

passages.text: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.
passages.original: Ἠλίας ἄνθρωπος ἦν ὁμοιοπαθὴς ἡμῖν καὶ προσευχῇ προσηύξατο τοῦ μὴ βρέξαι καὶ οὐκ ἔβρεξεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐνιαυτοὺς τρεῖς καὶ μῆνας ἕξ
passages.objections:
There's no way someone like me could ever have prayers that powerful.
Only special people or prophets can get God's attention like that.
God doesn't listen to ordinary folks when they pray.
Miracles like that only happened in the old days, not now.
I'm too flawed for my prayers to matter to God.
You have to be perfect or super holy for God to answer your prayers.
God only uses people who are completely different from us.
Prayer doesn't really change anything in the world.
If I pray, nothing big will ever happen because I'm just a regular person.

passages.text: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.
passages.original: καὶ πάλιν προσηύξατο καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ὑετὸν ἔδωκεν καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐβλάστησεν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτῆς
passages.objections:
Prayer doesn’t really change anything in the world.
Asking for rain is pointless—nature just does what it wants.
God doesn’t listen to ordinary people’s prayers about the weather.
Miracles like rain coming after prayer only happened in old stories, not now.
If the land is dry, there’s nothing anyone can do about it.
It’s just a coincidence if it rains after someone prays.
No one can influence what happens in the sky by praying.
God is too busy to care about small things like crops or rain.
Only special prophets could ever get answers to their prayers, not regular folks.

passages.text: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back, consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.
passages.original: Ἀδελφοί μου ἐάν τις ἐν ὑμῖν πλανηθῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἐπιστρέψῃ τις αὐτόν γινωσκέτω ὅτι ὁ ἐπιστρέψας ἁμαρτωλὸν ἐκ πλάνης ὁδοῦ αὐτοῦ σώσει ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐκ θανάτου καὶ καλύψει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν
passages.objections:
If someone strays from the truth, there’s no point trying to help them—they’re lost for good.
It’s not my responsibility if someone else falls into error; they have to find their own way back.
Once a person has sinned too much, there’s nothing anyone can do to help them.
Trying to correct someone who’s gone astray is just a waste of time.
People can’t really change, so why bother reaching out to them?
If someone leaves the faith, it’s better to just let them go and not get involved.
Helping a sinner return won’t make any real difference for their soul.
It’s not possible to cover over many sins just by helping someone turn back.
Only perfect people can help others; I’m not qualified to bring anyone back.
God doesn’t care if we try to help those who have wandered away.
